designation: CLOSE. Not a generation. The closing ruling of 2026-08-26, issued after G10, ends the technical work: one arithmetic check over artefacts that already existed, one rule enacted, one bound direction carried through the claim surface, and the spine as the measurements now support it. There is no generation 11.
termination_condition: T-1 was reached at generation 6. G7-R, G8, G9 and G10 were bounded generations ordered post-termination; each opened no new scientific scope and each was followed by another, which is why this file records `closed` as well as `terminated`. The closing ruling forbids a further generation by name -- no G11, no S-5, no S-2, no fourth chart, no minimum-energy path -- and permits exactly one check, constrained to arithmetic over existing artefacts. That check ran, needed no solve, and is recorded under `free_check`.

schema.champion_commit: The last CONTENT commit, by definition. Never the commit that wrote this file: a state file cannot name its own commit, because its bytes are part of the tree that commit hashes. Guarded by tests/test_loop_state_close.py.
schema.bookkeeping_commit: null at write time, always. Nothing may fill this during the commit that writes the file, because the value would be that commit's own hash.
schema.machinery_commit: Equal to champion_commit at close. The distinction between the tree a measurement ran against and the tree carrying its results does not arise here: nothing was measured. The inputs are pinned by SHA-256 in each artefact's `provenance` block instead, which is a stronger statement than a commit for a step that solved nothing.
schema.baselines: REP-01 as amended at generation 9 section 3: every entry is an OBJECT carrying the invocation that produced it, never a bare scalar. Entries marked rerunnable are re-run and compared; entries that are not carry conditions and measured_at_commit instead.
schema.free_check: The one measurement the closing ruling section 5 permits. Recorded separately from `spec_clause_status` because it is a DESCRIPTION and not a clause: it was ordered after the data existed, so no pre-registration is possible and none is claimed.

one_tree_one_commit.note: Vacuously, and the vacuity is the point: no solve ran at close, so there is no tree a measurement could disagree with. What replaces it is per-input attestation -- outputs/close/spectrum_shape.json and outputs/close/wit02_register.json each carry a SHA-256 for every file they read, so the arithmetic is pinned to bytes rather than to a commit. git_dirty is recorded beside it and deliberately not gated: a dirty tree cannot change an input whose digest is pinned.

free_check.question: does the rank climb 1 -> 4 over bias-window width come from sigma_2..sigma_4 RISING with width, or from sigma_1 FALLING so that a fixed absolute cutoff moves relative to a fixed spectrum shape?
free_check.status: DESCRIPTION, not a test. The question was asked after the spectra were on disk (AH-14). What stands in place of a pre-registration: the decomposition is an identity with no free parameter, the answer is a sign rather than a threshold so PH-11 has no cutoff to forbid, and the control axis was fixed by SPEC-g9-2's design a generation earlier.
free_check.arithmetic_only_is_checkable: tests/test_spectrum_shape_close.py::TestThisRanNoSolver parses scripts/run_close.py's AST and fails if it imports or calls anything that can reach the oracle. The guard is written over the AST and not over the text because the module's own docstring names the package in the sentence saying it does not import it.
free_check.result: The head is nearly fixed: sigma_1 moves by a factor of 1.195 and 1.148 across the nine widths and moves DOWNWARD, spearman -1.000 and -0.983, which is the wrong direction to raise a count against a cutoff that does not scale with it. The trailing values rise: sigma_2, sigma_3 and sigma_4 by x47.5, x55.4 and x315 at the generation-8 device and x20.9, x87.1 and x535 at device_p50, measured in the normalised spectrum, with 95.6% to 97.9% of each one's motion in the shape term of the identity. The spectrum's log-decay slope halves, -1.265 -> -0.552 and -1.261 -> -0.525, and the largest multiplicative gap behind the head collapses from 230.6x to 4.99x and from 87.8x to 5.11x. The rank climb is the spectrum FLATTENING, not the head sliding.

controls.C1: PASS -- generation 9's and generation 10's width curves are bit-identical, so the rank(cutoff) curves and the singular values belong to one spectrum.
controls.C2: PASS -- at the operational cutoff the rank is the raw count above it in all eighteen cells, not the resolvable_rank cap.
controls.C3: PASS at sigma_1..sigma_4, worst margin x1.51, and it FAILED at sigma_5 in four of the eighteen cells. The claim was narrowed rather than the control loosened; the excluded cells stay named in the artefact and tests/test_spectrum_shape_close.py keeps them named.
controls.C4: PASS -- alpha=0 and width=0.75 are one observation set reached by two code paths and their spectra agree exactly, and along the whole spacing axis, where the rank does not move, the decay slope moves 2.1% and 2.8% against width's 56% and 58%.

free_check.not_a_property_of_the_cutoff: The rank climbs and is non-decreasing in width in all ten device-cutoff sequences at the five cutoffs where resolvable_rank does not cap the count. Which cutoffs those are is measured, by recounting #{sigma > cutoff} and comparing, not chosen.
free_check.what_it_does_not_say: why the spectrum flattens. MECH-01 stays open, one step narrower: not 'why does the window set the rank' and not 'why is v_1 fixed while the others cross', but why does widening the bias window compress the sensitivity spectrum toward its own leading direction.

spec_clause_status.WIT-02: ENACTED, closing ruling section 2, and its live consequence is a registered non-compliance rather than a repair. 'Every witness is refined before it is counted -- not the ones near the floor, all of them.' No threshold, because the observed split sits between 92.2% and 93.65% of the distinguishability floor, a band 1.4 percentage points wide, and a threshold chosen inside it is tuned whatever its author intended (PH-11). The register is MEASURED -- outputs/close/wit02_register.json matches each refinement record to its witness pair on exact equality of the separation in decades against WIT-01's max_separation -- and it reports chart_G_d4 refined 3 of 13 with all 3 surviving, chart_L_d16 refined 0 of 37, chart_J_d16 refined 13 of 13 with 7 surviving. One committed set of three is compliant. Refining the other two is new solving, which the closing ruling section 5 forbids, so the gap is published rather than closed. Enacting the rule changed four claim-surface documents, one of which said 'all tested pairs survive 4x grid refinement' of a set in which three of thirteen pairs had ever been tested -- a sentence that is true and reads as its opposite.
spec_clause_status.WIT-01: UNCHANGED and NOT WITHDRAWN. It stays for the sub-grid case it does catch. Retro-applied it removes nothing: the admissibility ratio is 1.000 in all three charts, because every pair qualifies on a doping magnitude and magnitude coordinates reach the grid exactly. What it catches is one reported quantity, a chart-J pair's junction separation of 0.425 nm against a 3.333 nm node, which is withdrawn.
spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-1: UNCHANGED as a measurement; its gap is now DESCRIBED and still unexplained. The falsifier fired: the leading right singular vector's spread moves by 0.0080 and 0.0117 on a 0.0625-1.000 scale while the rank climbs 1 -> 4, spearman -0.433 and -1.000 against a registered threshold of >= +0.7, and the junction distance moves away from the junction. The closing ruling's free check adds what does move -- the spectrum flattens -- without adding why.
spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-2: UNCHANGED as a measurement and AMENDED in what it establishes. The classifier's output is unmoved: chart L at d=16 is 0 of 37 within the floor barrier and chart J at d=16 is 0 of 13, so the only cell putting pairs at the floor is chart G at d=4 and the split follows the DIMENSION. What changes is the reading of the two d=16 cells: the barrier is an UPPER bound, so each is a search that found no connecting path below the floor along the straight line, not a demonstration that the members are separated. The dimension ordering survives because both sides of the comparison are upper bounds; what is untested is whether the slack differs between cells.

The adopted range V in [0.15, 0.90] is stated with its source; the lower boundary is measured and rejected below, the upper one is UNTESTED (PH-15) because the convergence sweep's own upper end is 0.9 V, checked across every bias list in every artefact under outputs/.

open_findings.note: Narrowed once more at close, by arithmetic rather than by measurement. Generation 10 killed the localisation mechanism and left the question 'why is the leading direction fixed while the ones behind it cross the noise floor'. The free check answers the descriptive half: the leading direction is not merely fixed, it is FALLING -- by a factor of 1.195 and 1.148, spearman -1.000 and -0.983 -- which is the wrong direction to raise a count against an absolute cutoff, and the climb is carried entirely by the trailing values rising toward it. 95.6% to 97.9% of each trailing value's motion is in the normalised spectrum. So the phenomenon is the spectrum FLATTENING, and the open question is why widening the bias window compresses the sensitivity spectrum toward its own leading direction. Nothing here answers that and the ruling forbids chasing it.

open_findings.status: OPEN, AND ITS CONSEQUENCE IS NOW PAID
open_findings.note: Unchanged as a finding; what changed is that its consequence has been taken rather than noted. Every barrier walks a straight line in that chart's own coordinates, so every depth is an UPPER bound. The closing ruling section 3 follows that all the way: it STRENGTHENS the chart-G ridge, whose true barrier is then at most at the floor, and WEAKENS both d=16 results to search statements -- no connecting path below the floor was found along the straight line, which is not separation. The test that would settle it is a minimum-energy path, string method or NEB against the same oracle with the same floor barrier as the criterion. It was not run and is out of budget. AH-13 applies in its usual direction.

Generation 9 put chart J's 13 pairs through that battery and 6 of 13 separated, so the direction of the risk is known even though its size is not. WIT-02 does not resolve this -- it registers it, with the coverage measured rather than recalled: outputs/close/wit02_register.json.

'The geometry of the degeneracy is chart-dependent' stays withdrawn. What replaces it is amended in one word: the two d=16 cells are cells in which no path below the floor was FOUND, so 'basin' names the observed shape and not a demonstrated separation.

highest_remaining_scientific_risk: The mechanism question is open and the close describes it rather than answering it. The rank climb is the sensitivity spectrum flattening -- the head nearly fixed and falling, the trailing values rising toward it, 95.6% to 97.9% of the motion in shape -- and nothing in this repository says why widening a bias window does that. The description is worth having because it rules out the remaining cheap explanation: the head does not slide, so no account that works by moving the leading singular value can be right.
second_remaining_scientific_risk: PATH-01, whose consequence is now paid rather than pending. Every barrier is a straight line in one chart's coordinates and therefore an upper bound, so both d=16 results are searches that found no connecting path below the floor rather than demonstrations of separation. A minimum-energy path -- string method or NEB against the same oracle -- is the measurement that would settle it and was not run.
third_remaining_scientific_risk: WITNESS-04, now registered under WIT-02. The 37 chart-L witness pairs that carry the dimension reading have never been refined; in the one comparable set that was refined in full, 6 of 13 separated. The direction of the error is not obvious and is not guessed at.
